title: Winter Swimming in Berlin - Quick Summary
kicker: WALK OF BERLIN • LIVING IN BERLIN
items: **Swimming stays legal in winter wherever it is legal in summer.** The 15 May to 15 September season only decides when the water is tested.
**The Spree, every canal and the Havel from Eiswerder to Schildhorn are banned all year,** as are bridges (100 m), ferry piers (50 m) and shipping channels.

**Orankesee, Weißer See and Plötzensee are bathing water only inside their lidos,** which are closed until spring. Schlachtensee, Krumme Lanke, Wannsee and the Müggelsee are listed as whole lakes or free shores.
**Last winter most lakes dropped under 10 °C between 27 October and 17 November,** under 4 °C by late December, and only climbed back above 8 °C between 10 and 24 March.
**Never swim alone, walk in slowly and stay in a minute or less as a beginner.** Dry off and dress at once; the dizziness often comes after you get out.
**Public dates:** Eisfasching at Strandbad Orankesee on the second Saturday of January and the Großes Eisbaden at Seebad Friedrichshagen on 17 January 2027 (€15 presale).
**Ice rule from DLRG Berlin:** step onto a lake only at 15 cm of ice, onto a river at 20 cm, never alone. If someone goes through, call 112 and help from the shore.
